sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic laws part two: backing safely, parking rules and hill parking, highway parking, seat belts and exemptions, child restraints, airbags and hand position, what to do after a crash, insurance and registration, and wireless device limits
Knowledge domain: how to back up and park legally, where parking is forbidden, how to secure every passenger, what the law requires after a crash, the insurance and registration duties of a Minnesota vehicle owner, and the limits on using a phone while driving.

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Before you back up, walk around the vehicle to be sure nothing is behind it, and look to the front, both sides and the rear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the edge of the road may be no more than 12 inches from the curb. [A01]
Why it matters: the curb distance is a classic numeric item.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
After parallel parking, point the front wheels toward the curb or shoulder, shift into park and set the parking brake, so a vehicle that starts rolling heads for the curb rather than a traffic lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Parking is forbidden inside an intersection and on a crosswalk or sidewalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
You may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
You may not park within 30 feet of a flashing light, stop sign or traffic control signal standing beside a public road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
You may not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
You may not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant. [A01]
Why it matters: the hydrant distance is easy to swap with the crosswalk and signal distances.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
When stopped or parked at the roadside, check for approaching vehicles, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians before opening any door, and keep a traffic-side door open only as long as loading or unloading needs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
When a parked vehicle faces downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or the road's shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
When a parked vehicle faces uphill next to a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
When a parked vehicle faces uphill where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, level with it and roughly one and a half feet away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A03
A vehicle parked on a highway at night, or whenever lights are needed, must show at least one white or amber front light and one red taillight, each visible from at least 500 feet. [A03]
Why it matters: the visibility distance for a parked vehicle's lights is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A03
Every person in the vehicle, front and back, must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, and an officer may stop a driver for a seat belt violation alone. [A03]
Why it matters: a stop for the belt alone is a common test item.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A03
Riding without a seat belt makes you four times more likely to be killed or injured in a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A03
An unbelted occupant can die in a crash at speeds as low as 12 mph. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A03
The belt law does not apply to someone driving a passenger vehicle in reverse, to a rider whose seat belts are all taken by other passengers, or to a person holding a doctor's written certificate for medical reasons. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A03
Workers whose job means getting in and out of the vehicle often are exempt from wearing a belt only while they drive no faster than 25 mph. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A03
Wear the lap belt snug across the hipbones or upper thighs and never across the soft part of the stomach, and the shoulder belt snug across the chest and the middle of the shoulder, using both together. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A04
Children younger than 13 must ride in the back seat whenever a back seat is available. [A04]
Why it matters: the back seat age is a likely test item.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A04
Car seats and booster seats must be federally approved and installed the way the manufacturer instructs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A04
A child under 2 rides rear-facing until reaching the seat's height or weight limit, and a child who turns 2 while still within those limits keeps riding rear-facing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A04
A child older than 2 who has outgrown the rear-facing limits rides in a forward-facing car seat until reaching its limit, which is usually 40 to 60 pounds depending on the maker. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A04
A child aged 4 to 9 who has outgrown the car seat must use a booster seat together with a safety belt. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A04
At age 9, or once a child exceeds the booster seat's height or weight limit, the child rides without the booster but buckled in a seat belt. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A04
Child restraints expire six years after they are made unless a different date is stamped on the seat, and a seat that has been in a crash should not be used again. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A05
An airbag is a supplemental restraint system that helps a seat belt prevent injuries but is not built to stop you from being thrown out. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A05
Keep at least 10 inches between your body and the steering wheel. [A05]
Why it matters: the airbag spacing distance is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A05
Hold the wheel at the 8 and 4 or the 9 and 3 o'clock positions with thumbs turned outward, and avoid the 10 and 2 o'clock position. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A05
After a crash, stop, move out of the driving lane onto the shoulder if you can, and switch off the ignition to lower the fire risk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A05
Warn approaching drivers of a crash scene with emergency flashers, flares or a flashlight. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A05
If anyone is hurt or killed in the crash, call the nearest law enforcement agency or 911 as fast as you can. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A05
The law requires you to give crash victims reasonable assistance, giving first aid if you are able and qualified, or otherwise keeping the injured comfortable. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A05
Give the other drivers and any officer at the scene your name, address, date of birth and vehicle registration number, and show your driver's license to anyone who asks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A05
If asked, give your insurer's name and address and your agent's name, and if you do not have them with you, provide them within 72 hours. [A05]
Why it matters: the insurance deadline is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A05
A crash that damages only property does not have to be reported to law enforcement, but tow a disabled vehicle quickly and tell the owner of any other property you damaged. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A06
An owner whose vehicle is driven on public roads must carry no-fault and liability insurance and keep valid proof of it in the vehicle at all times. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A06
Not producing proof of insurance when an officer asks can lead to revocation of your driver's license and your vehicle registration. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A06
To get driving privileges back after an insurance revocation, you take and pass a written test, pay a $30 reinstatement fee on top of any court fines or citations, apply for a new license and file an insurance certificate from your insurer. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A06
A conviction for driving an uninsured vehicle can bring a fine of up to $1,000 and up to 90 days in jail, and driving privileges may be revoked for up to one year. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A06
A new Minnesota resident has up to 60 days to register each vehicle driven on public roads with DVS. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A06
While driving you may not use a phone or other wireless device to write, read or send emails, texts or instant messages, or to go online. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A06
The messaging ban does not cover calling for emergency help, reporting a crash or crime, or using the device in voice-activated or hands-free mode. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A06
A driver convicted two or more times of messaging while driving must pay a $275 fine on top of the fine the court sets. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

Misconceptions: on an uphill slope with a curb the wheels turn away from the curb, not toward it; a crash with only property damage does not need a police report, but injuries or deaths always need a call; airbags do not replace seat belts; the hands-free exception does not allow reading or typing messages.
Mnemonics: hydrant ten, crosswalk twenty, signal thirty, railroad fifty; downhill and uphill without a curb turn toward the edge, uphill with a curb turn away; under two rear-facing, four to nine booster, under thirteen in the back.
Glossary: no-fault insurance means one of the two coverage types every owner of a vehicle driven on Minnesota public roads must carry; liability insurance means coverage for property damage and injuries to other people; double parking means stopping on the traffic side of a vehicle already parked at the curb or road edge; deputy registrar means the local office where you bring your title and identification to register a vehicle; supplemental restraint system means a device such as an airbag that works together with the seat belt.
Dynamic facts: the reinstatement fee, the uninsured-vehicle fine and jail caps and the repeat messaging fine are amounts set by law that can change, and the Office of Traffic Safety web address printed in the chapter may move; recheck them against DVS before each release.
